description: Figure 6(a) is a grouped bar chart illustrating the annual distribution of datasets from 2012 to 2022, categorized by the geographic location of the researchers. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100). The horizontal axis represents the year. Each year contains a group of colored bars corresponding to six categories in the legend: “Other” (blue), “UK” (red), “USA” (orange), “IT” (purple), “IN” (green), and “DE” (brown). The chart shows that datasets from the USA (orange) are consistently among the highest each year, often exceeding 10 datasets and peaking above 100 in 2020 and 2021. Researchers from “Other” locations (blue) also contribute significantly, with values frequently surpassing 10 and reaching over 100 in 2020 and 2021. Contributions from the UK, Italy, India, and Germany are generally lower and more variable, with most years showing fewer than 10 datasets per country. The caption notes that researchers from the US publish most consistently, while other countries began producing more datasets since 2016 — a trend visible in the rising bars for countries like India and Germany after that year.
